newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA says economy too firm for rate cut.
newsitem.headline: CBA says economy too firm for rate cut.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA), which has Australia's largest home loan portfolio, believes there are enough signs the economy is strengthening to make another rate cut premature.

"I think that we have started down a stronger growth path. All of our internal indicators point to continuing stronger growth signals and therefore it may be premature for us to consider a rate cut," CBA Managing Director David Murray told reporters after an address to a Committee for Economic Development of Australia (CEDA) luncheon.
He had been asked if continuing low inflation data would allow the Reserve Bank of Australia to lower official cash rates again from their current 6.0 percent.
Earlier, the Australian Bureau of Statistics released data showing underlying inflation rose 0.4 percent in the March quarter, keeping annual underlying inflation steady at 2.1 percent.
Some economists have said the inflation result, although in line with expectations, removed another obstacle to a fourth rate cut within a year.
Most economists, however, saw rates staying on hold for most of this year before a rate hike possibly in late 1997 or more probably early 1998.
The RBA cut official rates from 7.5 percent to the current 6.0 percent in three separate 50 basis point chunks in the second half of last year.
Murray said the Australian dollar had also not been particulary strong.
"Putting all that together, my expectation is for interest rates to remain where there are for some time yet," he said.
